extracted.intended_audience: writers, contributors, and readers of The Paris Review (potential submitters and literary community)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes The Paris Review's editorial mission and selection preferences—what the magazine values in submissions and its broader publishing goals, including emphasis on creative work and long-form author interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on creative work—fiction and poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Paris Review hopes to emphasize creative work—fiction and poetry—not to the exclusion of criticism, but with the aim in mind of merely removing criticism from the dominating place it holds in most literary magazines and putting it pretty much where it belongs, i.e., somewhere near the back of the book.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize original creative writing (fiction and poetry) over criticism; accept criticism only in a secondary, de-emphasized role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of criticism (de-emphasized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism should not dominate the magazine and should be placed near the back of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical pieces are allowed but the editorial preference is to relegate them to a less prominent position compared with creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcome good writers and good poets; avoid agitational voices
rubrics_metrics.description: “I think The Paris Review should welcome these people into its pages: the good writers and good poets, the non-drumbeaters and non-axe-grinders. So long as they're good.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors high-quality writing and a certain literary temperament—work that is strong in craft rather than attention-seeking, polemical, or 'drumbeating'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce and publish important/new writers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review has historically introduced important writers (examples: Adrienne Rich, Philip Roth, V. S. Naipaul, Jack Kerouac, Italo Calvino, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorially values work that may mark significant literary contributions or notable early appearances by emerging writers; the magazine positions itself as a discoverer of important literary voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value long-form author interviews (Writers at Work series)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Review’s Writers at Work interview series offers authors a rare opportunity to discuss their life and art at length; they have responded with some of the most revealing self-portraits in literature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine prizes in-depth interviews that allow authors to explain craft and life—content that provides substantive insight into process and artistic values.
